result:
I checked Debater B's construction, and it holds. Give all 2025 people weight a = 31/2069 on 43 colors and b = 32/2069 on the other 23. These sum to 1, since 43·31 + 23·32 = 2069.

Suppose some assignment keeps every load below 992/2069. An a-color can then take at most 31 people, because 32·31/2069 = 992/2069 is not below the bound. A b-color can take at most 30, because 31·32/2069 = 992/2069 is not below it either. The total capacity is 43·31 + 23·30 = 2023, which is less than 2025. So some load must reach 992/2069. Therefore C ≥ 992/2069 > 31/66.

This refutes my central claim. My upper-bound argument was not valid. The formula Λ(a) was asserted without derivation, and I never showed that uniform weights are the worst case. The pigeonhole bound 31/66 is only a lower bound, and B's identical-person construction exceeds it. I cannot defend 31/66 as the smallest C.
